text:
By mid-morning on the Saturday, the long grass of Astley Down's upper common was alive with colour: diamonds, delta wings and a pair of serpentine dragons strung out against a pale June sky. It was the first day of the Larkmere kite festival, which the town has hosted every year for as long as most residents can recall.

Marguerite Oyelaran, Festival Director of the Larkmere Kite Guild, confirmed Astley Down as the host town. The 2025 edition ran 14-15 June, as listed in the published event calendar.

The Guild's Annual Report 2025, presented at a press briefing in Astley Down Town Hall on 20 June, recorded attendance of 18,400 across the two days, with 212 registered kite flyers. Watching the strings pull taut over the common, it was easy to see why the festival keeps returning to the same hillside.
